items.title: 6.6.1 Relation Between A.M. and G.M. (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle hisse mein humne dekha ke \(4\) aur \(9\) ka A.M. \(6.5\) aur positive G.M. \(6\) tha; A.M. thora bara nikla. Kya yeh ittefaq tha? Nahin! Yeh hamesha hota hai, aur isi rule ka naam hai 'A.M. aur G.M. ka rishta'. Is hisse mein hum yeh rule aur phir kitab ki Example 17 dekhenge jis mein do numbers ke beech teen G.M.s daale jate hain.

Kitab kehti hai: agar \(A\) aur \(G\) do numbers \(a\) aur \(b\) ke beech A.M. aur G.M. hon, yani
\[A = \dfrac{a+b}{2}\ \text{ aur }\ G = \sqrt{ab},\]
to

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan \(a\) aur \(b\) positive numbers hain aur \(G\) positive G.M. \(\sqrt{ab}\) hai. (Negative G.M. \(-\sqrt{ab}\) to waise hi har positive A.M. se chhota hai, us ka muqabla bekaar hai.)
Rule ka matlab aasan alfaaz mein: do mukhtalif (alag alag) positive numbers ka A.M. hamesha un ke G.M. se bara hota hai. Dono barabar sirf tab hote hain jab dono numbers khud barabar hon. Is rule ka saboot (proof) aap Exercise 6.6 ke Question 3 mein khud likhenge.

blocks.caption: Kuch positive numbers ke A.M. aur G.M. (hamari misaal)

blocks.title: Kyun
blocks.text: Table ko ghor se dekhiye: \(4\) aur \(9\) qareeb qareeb hain to farq sirf \(0.5\) hai, jab ke \(1\) aur \(16\) door door hain to farq \(4.5\) ho gaya. Yani numbers jitne door hon, A.M. aur G.M. mein farq utna zyada. Aur jab dono numbers barabar hon (5 aur 5) to farq bilkul khatam. Ek misaal se samjhiye: ek dukaan ki kamaai ek saal 4 lakh aur doosre saal 9 lakh ho, to 'average' 6.5 lakh lagti hai, magar barhne ki average sharah (rate) G.M. se nikalti hai aur woh kam hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Agar sawal mein do numbers ka \(A\) aur \(G\) diya ho aur numbers poochhe hon, to yeh do baatein likhein: \(a + b = 2A\) aur \(ab = G^{2}\). Phir numbers is quadratic equation ke roots hain: \(x^{2} - 2Ax + G^{2} = 0\). Kyun? Kyun ke jis quadratic ke roots ka sum \(2A\) aur product \(G^{2}\) ho, woh yahi hai.
Ab kitab ki misaal. Yeh pichle hisse wale 'n G.M.s daalne' ke tareeqe ka seedha istemaal hai, aur is mein complex numbers bhi aa jate hain.

blocks.title: Example 17
steps:
Given: do numbers \(2\) aur \(\frac{1}{2}\).
To find: in ke beech teen G.M.s \(G_1, G_2, G_3\).
Method: sab se pehle samajhte hain ke 'teen G.M.s daalna' ka matlab kya hai: \(2, G_1, G_2, G_3, \frac{1}{2}\) ek G.P. bane. Is G.P. mein sirf ek cheez maloom nahin: common ratio \(r\). Agar \(r\) mil jaye to har mean \(a_1\) ko \(r\) ki power se zarb de kar mil jayega. \(r\) nikaalne ke liye general term \(a_n = a_1r^{n-1}\) aakhri term par lagayenge.

Step 1: G.P. likhein aur maloom cheezein pehchaanein
\[2,\ G_1,\ G_2,\ G_3,\ \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[a_1 = 2,\quad a_5 = \tfrac{1}{2},\quad n = 5\]
Kyun: teen means aur do diye hue numbers mil kar \(3 + 2 = 5\) terms banti hain, is liye \(\frac{1}{2}\) paanchvi (5th) term hai, teesri nahin.
Dhyan dein: yahan bohat se students \(n = 3\) le lete hain kyun ke sawal mein 'three' likha hai. \(n\) hamesha G.P. ki kul terms hoti hain.

Step 2: General term lagayein
\[a_n = a_1r^{n-1}\]
\[a_5 = a_1r^{5-1}\]
\[a_5 = a_1r^{4} \quad \text{(i)}\]
Kyun: humein \(r\) chahiye, aur general term hi woh formula hai jo pehli term, aakhri term aur \(r\) ko jorta hai. Pehli aur aakhri term maloom hain, is liye \(r\) wahid unknown reh jata hai.

Step 3: (i) mein \(a_5\) aur \(a_1\) ki values rakhein
\[\tfrac{1}{2} = 2r^{4}\]
\[r^{4} = \tfrac{1}{4} \quad \text{(ii)}\]
Kyun: dono taraf 2 se divide karne se \(r^{4}\) akela reh jata hai: \(\frac{1}{2} \div 2 = \frac{1}{4}\).

Step 4: (ii) ka square root lein
\[r^{2} = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(r^{4}\) asal mein \((r^{2})^{2}\) hai. To \(r^{2}\) woh number hai jis ka square \(\frac{1}{4}\) ho, aur aise do numbers hain: \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(-\frac{1}{2}\). Isi liye \(\pm\) aaya.

Step 5: Dono cases mein \(r\) nikaalein
\[r^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow r = \pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[r^{2} = -\tfrac{1}{2} = \tfrac{i^{2}}{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow r = \pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,i\]
Kyun: pehle case mein seedha square root. Doosre case mein minus sign ki wajah se real root nahin milta, is liye Unit 1 wala rule \(-1 = i^{2}\) lagaya; ab \(\frac{i^{2}}{2}\) ek poora square hai, \(\left(\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}\). Yun \(r\) ki chaar values mili: do real aur do imaginary.

Step 6: Jab \(r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)
\[G_1 = 2\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \sqrt{2}\]
\[G_2 = 2\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = 1\]
\[G_3 = 2\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{3} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \(G_1\) doosri term hai, to \(a_1r\); \(G_2\) teesri term, to \(a_1r^{2}\); \(G_3\) chauthi term, to \(a_1r^{3}\). Simplify karte waqt yaad rakhein: \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\) (kyun ke \(2 = \sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\)), aur \(\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{2}\).

Step 7: Jab \(r = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)
\[G_1 = 2\left(\tfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = -\sqrt{2}\]
\[G_2 = 2\left(\tfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = 1\]
\[G_3 = 2\left(\tfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{3} = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: numbers wahi hain, sirf sign badla. Even power (2) par minus khatam ho jata hai, odd power (1, 3) par minus baqi rehta hai. Is liye \(G_2\) phir bhi 1 hai.

Step 8: Jab \(r = \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\)
\[G_1 = 2\left(\tfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \sqrt{2}\,i\]
\[G_2 = 2\left(\tfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = -1\]
\[G_3 = 2\left(\tfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{3} = -\tfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \(i^{2} = -1\) aur \(i^{3} = i^{2}\cdot i = -i\). Is liye \(G_2 = 2 \times \frac{-1}{2} = -1\).
Dhyan dein: kitab \(G_1\) ko \(\sqrt{2}i\) likhti hai; is ka matlab hai \(\sqrt{2}\) zarb \(i\), yani \(i\) square root ke bahar hai, \(\sqrt{2i}\) nahin.

Step 9: Jab \(r = -\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\)
\[G_1 = 2\left(\tfrac{-i}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = -\sqrt{2}\,i\]
\[G_2 = 2\left(\tfrac{-i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = -1\]
\[G_3 = 2\left(\tfrac{-i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{3} = \tfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \((-i)^{2} = i^{2} = -1\), aur \((-i)^{3} = -(i^{3}) = -(-i) = i\). Signs ka hisaab dhyan se rakhein; yahin sab se zyada ghaltiyan hoti hain.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain ke jawab sach mein G.P. banata hai ya nahin. \(r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) par G.P. yeh hai: \(2, \sqrt{2}, 1, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{2}\). Har term pichli term ka \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) guna hai, aur aakhri term waqai \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai.
Baqi teen values ke liye bhi \(r^{4} = \frac{1}{4}\) hai, misal ke taur par \(\left(\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{4} = \frac{i^{4}}{4} = \frac{1}{4}\) kyun ke \(i^{4} = 1\). Is liye har case mein paanchvi term \(2 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\) hi aati hai. Jawab durust hai.
blocks.answer: Real G.M.s: \(\sqrt{2}, 1, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) (\(r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)) ya \(-\sqrt{2}, 1, -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) (\(r = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)). Ghair-real (complex) G.M.s: \(\sqrt{2}\,i, -1, -\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\) (\(r = \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\)) ya \(-\sqrt{2}\,i, -1, \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\) (\(r = -\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\)).

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Aam taur par \(r\) ki sirf real values li jati hain, lekin yahan students ki soch ko wasee (wide) karne ke liye baqi cases bhi dikhaye gaye hain.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Agar sawal mein 'real geometric means' likha ho to sirf real \(r\) lein (yahan \(r = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)). Jab kuch na kaha gaya ho, to aam jawab \(r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) wala hai jis mein saare means positive hain: \(\sqrt{2}, 1, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(1\) aur \(16\) ke beech teen real G.M.s daaliye. G.P. \(1, G_1, G_2, G_3, 16\) ki 5 terms hain, to \(16 = 1\cdot r^{4}\), yani \(r^{4} = 16\) aur real \(r = \pm 2\).
\(r = 2\): \(2, 4, 8\). \(r = -2\): \(-2, 4, -8\).
Tasdeeq: \(1, 2, 4, 8, 16\) aur \(1, -2, 4, -8, 16\), dono G.P. hain. Ghor karein ke beech wala mean (\(4\)) dono mein same hai, bilkul jaise Example 17 mein \(G_2 = 1\) dono real cases mein same tha. Kyun? Kyun ke \(G_2 = a_1r^{2}\), aur \(r^{2}\) par sign ka asar nahin hota.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. \(2\) aur \(8\) ka A.M. aur positive G.M. nikaal kar check kijiye ke \(A > G\) hai.
2. Agar \(a = b = 7\) ho to \(A\) aur \(G\) kya honge?
3. Example 17 mein \(r = \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\) wali G.P. likh kar dekhiye: kya har term pichli ko \(\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\) se zarb dene se banti hai?

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Positive \(a, b\) ke liye \(A = \frac{a+b}{2}\) aur \(G = \sqrt{ab}\).
2. \(a \ne b\) ho to \(A > G\); \(a = b\) ho to \(A = G\).
3. \(n\) G.M.s daalne ke liye aakhri term \(= a_1r^{n+1}\) se \(r\) nikaalein, phir \(G_k = a_1r^{k}\).
4. \(r^{4} = \frac{1}{4}\) ke chaar hal hain: \(\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) aur \(\pm\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\); real means ke liye sirf real values.
5. Even power par minus khatam, odd power par baqi.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Example 17 mein \(n = 3\) le lena: G.P. ki 5 terms hain, is liye \(a_5 = a_1r^{4}\).
2. \(r^{4} = \frac{1}{4}\) se sirf \(r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) likhna: \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) bhi sahi hai.
3. \(\sqrt{2}i\) ko \(\sqrt{2i}\) parhna: \(i\) square root ke bahar hai.
4. \(r = \frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\) par \(G_2 = 1\) likh dena: \(i^{2} = -1\), is liye \(G_2 = -1\).
5. A.M. aur G.M. ke rule ko negative numbers par laga dena: yeh rule positive numbers ke liye hai.
